paper_title: SEP-NMPC: Safety Enhanced Passivity-Based Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for a UAV Slung Payload System
selection_reason: The paper explicitly studies a single quadrotor with a suspended payload and gives the complete outer-loop model, NMPC problem, passivity inequality, and HOCBF equations.

The original outer-loop decision is a 3D translational force and the paper explicitly assumes an attitude-thrust inner loop, so the x component can be converted to the frozen x-acceleration interface without replacing GeometricInnerLoop.
The paper's 2 s / 40-node discretization is compatible with a 20 Hz outer-loop implementation; the current benchmark can enforce the already frozen acceleration and slew limits.
The method is selected before any controller implementation or performance experiment; future performance on the current five-link plant is unknown.
main_strengths: Passivity-based swing-energy dissipation embedded directly in the predictive optimization.
Explicit payload-aware HOCBF formulation and formal stability/safety argument.
Reported simulation and real-world experiments in the original paper.
main_model_gaps: Original model is a point mass on a massless rigid cable with two swing angles.
Current plant has five massive rigid links, damped/frictional hinges, a rigid 2.5 kg cutter, and distributed aerodynamic forces.
The paper does not specify a wind observer or future-wind feedforward contract; current adaptation must use nominal prediction and measured/history-only feedback.
adaptation_summary: Use a frozen planar reduced internal predictor and an equivalent cutter-tip/multi-link sway output, retain the paper's passivity-constrained NMPC structure, map its x force to ax_cmd, and evaluate the unchanged full five-link MuJoCo plant. This is a fair adaptation contract, not a claim that SEP-NMPC natively models five links.
license: No controller code identified; arXiv paper is distributed under the arXiv perpetual non-exclusive license.
